official.deadline_note: The 1 February - 1 April application window is fixed annually by Cabinet Regulation No. 68. VIAA's studies page currently displays the 2026/2027 round (open call 1 February 2026, deadline 1 April 2026; results announced 29 June 2026), so the next annual call for the 2027/2028 academic year is expected to open 1 February 2027 and close 1 April 2027.
official.application_cycle: Annual call, 1 February - 1 April, for the next academic year (2026/2027 round completed, results announced 29 June 2026; next cycle 2027/2028)
official.status_note: VIAA's studies page currently shows the 2026/2027 round, whose results were announced on 29 June 2026 (104 scholarships awarded to applicants from 22 nationalities out of 427 applications from 33 countries). The next call for the 2027/2028 academic year follows the fixed regulatory window of 1 February - 1 April.
official.tuition_coverage_note: VIAA states that all study programmes in English at Latvian higher education institutions are not free of charge and that the scholarship holder can use the scholarship for covering the tuition fee or for accommodation and meals, while stressing that the amount of the scholarship is not high enough to cover all expenses in Latvia. The stipend is not a tuition waiver.
benefits: EUR 500 per month for bachelor's and master's students (set under Cabinet Regulation No. 68 of 24 January 2012, as amended by Cabinet Regulation No. 298 of 26 May 2026)
EUR 700 per month for PhD students
Up to 10 months of funding per academic year for bachelor's and master's students; up to 11 months for doctoral students
In limited numbers, the host higher education institution provides the scholarship holder with a place in a students' dormitory or guesthouse
Separate strand funding participation in approved summer schools in Latvia, with funds transferred to the summer school organisers
eligibility: Citizens of countries that have signed an agreement on co-operation in education and science with Latvia, or countries that offer scholarships to Latvian students, researchers and teaching staff (39 eligible countries listed for 2026/2027: 28 agreement countries including Azerbaijan, China, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Poland, Turkey, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, plus 11 countries such as Austria, Czech Republic, Estonia, Germany, Hungary, Japan, Switzerland, the United States)

Bachelor's and first-level professional higher education applicants must have successfully completed at least one academic year of studies at any higher education institution at the moment of application
Master's or PhD students from any previous higher education institution
An applicant must choose a study programme at a Latvian higher education institution and receive the confirmation letter from the designated contact person of that institution before applying
Each applicant can submit only one application per open call
A scholarship cannot be awarded concurrently with other grants
An international student can receive the Latvian state scholarship for a maximum of two terms within one study cycle
Scholarships for applicants from one country may not exceed 10% of the total grant amount for study scholarships in the respective year
requirements: Register in the VIAA electronic application system and create a profile with a unique login and password
Fill in the online application form according to the published quality evaluation criteria; incomplete and incorrect applications are not assessed
Attach all required documents translated into Latvian or English
Submit the application in the system by the deadline of the call (1 February - 1 April)
Study programmes must be implemented in the official language of the country or another official language of the European Union
Applicants nominated by a competent authority of their country must also contact that authority and send application documents to it if required
A minimum of 11 points in the quality evaluation is required for the scholarship to be granted
documents: Copy of the confirmation letter from the Latvian higher education institution, prepared by the designated contact person on the unified template
Curriculum vitae in the Europass template
Letter of motivation, including activities outside studies related to the study field in Latvia or the home country
Proof of education: diploma and supplements, or transcript of records of the last two semesters; first-year master's students must provide their bachelor's diploma copy and its supplement
Copies of two letters of recommendation from academic staff members, signed within the last six months
Study plan for the scholarship period on the official form
Copy of a certificate or other document attesting the language proficiency required for the studies
Copy of a passport or identification card
selection_criteria: Administrative evaluation criteria assessed Yes/No: eligibility under an international agreement, required language proficiency, successful results in previous studies, and a complete application
Achievements in the past two semesters or according to the diploma (up to 5 points)
Justification of how the chosen studies in Latvia will improve knowledge and professional skills, including motivation for studying in Latvia (up to 5 points)
Extracurricular activities in Latvia and in the home country related to the chosen field of studies (up to 5 points)
Application to Latvian and Baltic philology, literature and culture or Latvian history (up to 5 points); 20 points in total, minimum 11 required
On equal scores, priority goes first to doctoral students, then to master's students; priority is also given to applicants nominated by an authorised authority of their country
coverage: Monthly stipend of EUR 500 for bachelor's and master's students
Monthly stipend of EUR 700 for doctoral students
Up to 10 months per academic year for bachelor's and master's students
Up to 11 months per academic year for doctoral students
The holder may spend the stipend on the tuition fee or on accommodation and meals; travel from the home country to and from Latvia, insurance and visa costs are not covered
application_method: Register in the electronic application system at scholarships.viaa.gov.lv and create a profile with a unique login and password
Complete the online application form following the published quality evaluation criteria

Upload the confirmation letter from the Latvian HEI, Europass CV, motivation letter, proof of education, two recommendation letters, study plan, language certificate and passport copy, translated into Latvian or English where needed

official.application_route: Online only, through the VIAA electronic application system (scholarships.viaa.gov.lv) during the annual call from 1 February to 1 April; no paper applications
official.citizenship_residency: Only citizens of the eligible countries listed annually by the Ministry of Education and Science may apply; for 2026/2027 the list comprises 39 countries (28 with signed co-operation agreements on co-operation in education and science plus 11 countries that offer scholarships to Latvian students without formal agreements). The list is published by 1 November each year.
official.international_eligibility: The scholarship is exclusively for foreign students from Latvia's partner countries; Latvian citizens and non-listed nationalities cannot apply
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field-of-study restriction for degree studies, but the programme must be taught in Latvian or another official EU language; a separate summer-school strand is limited to summer schools approved by VIAA, and applicants nominated by a competent authority of their home country must also apply through that authority
official.research_requirement: No research proposal is required; a study plan for the scholarship period must be submitted on the official form
official.duration: One academic year per award (up to 10 months for bachelor's and master's students, up to 11 months for doctoral students); a maximum of two terms within one study cycle; the Latvian academic year runs from 1 September to 30 June
official.description: The Latvian state scholarship for studies is a government stipend administered by the State Education Development Agency (VIAA) under Cabinet Regulation No. 68, supporting citizens of Latvia's partner countries to study at Latvian higher education institutions. It pays EUR 500 per month to bachelor's and master's students and EUR 700 per month to doctoral students for one academic year, applied for through a single annual online call from 1 February to 1 April. VIAA stresses that the scholarship does not cover all study-related expenses and cannot be combined with other grants.
official.program_type: Government scholarship (Latvian state scholarship for studies)
official.english_requirement: A copy of a certificate or other document attesting the language proficiency required for the studies is one of the mandatory application documents, and language proficiency is an administrative evaluation criterion; VIAA does not publish a specific test or minimum score

A specific English test or minimum score (only a language-proficiency certificate is required, no level or test is named)
Number of scholarships available for the next cycle (only the 2026/2027 outcome of 104 awards is published)

verification.notes: Amounts (EUR 500/month bachelor's and master's, EUR 700/month PhD), award duration, eligibility, documents, the 1 February - 1 April annual window and the evaluation criteria were verified on VIAA's own site (viaa.gov.lv/en/studies), on studyinlatvia.lv (VIAA's Study in Latvia portal) and against Cabinet Regulation No. 68 on likumi.lv. The VIAA studies page shows the figures in an image; the same amounts are stated in text on studyinlatvia.lv with the citation of the amending Cabinet Regulation No. 298 of 26 May 2026.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a monthly stipend of EUR 500 (EUR 700 for PhD) paid for up to 10 months a year, not a tuition waiver, so budget for the full tuition of your Latvian programme plus flights, insurance and visa yourself. The single annual window runs 1 February to 1 April through VIAA's online system, and everything hinges on getting a confirmation letter from a Latvian university before you can even submit. Because only one application per call is allowed and incomplete files are not assessed, treat the confirmation letter and the certified translations as the first tasks, not the last.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A citizen of one of the 39 partner countries who has already finished at least one year of higher education and holds a study place confirmed by a Latvian university
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is on the current eligible-country list before doing anything else (the list is republished by 1 November each year)

Pick your Latvian study programme early and email the institution's designated contact person to request the confirmation letter on VIAA's unified template; ask for it in January, months before the 1 April close
Prepare a Europass-format CV rather than a local template
Collect the two recommendation letters from academic staff within six months of submission so their signature dates stay valid
Have every non-English document translated into Latvian or English before the call opens
Register a profile in scholarships.viaa.gov.lv ahead of the deadline to test login and upload limits
common_rejection_risks: Missing or wrongly formatted HEI confirmation letter: only a letter from the designated contact person on the unified template is valid
Incomplete application: VIAA states incomplete and incorrect applications are not assessed at all, and administrative criteria are pass/fail
Weak motivation and extracurricular section: 10 of the 20 quality points come from justification of studying in Latvia and field-related activities outside studies
Below the 11-point threshold in the quality evaluation, or squeezed out by the 10% per-country quota in a year with many applicants from your nationality
Applying for bachelor's without having completed at least one full academic year of prior higher education
Recommendation letters signed more than six months before submission
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition (VIAA notes English-taught programmes typically run from EUR 2,800 to EUR 15,000 per year), travel to and from Latvia, health insurance, visa and residence permit costs, and any living costs beyond what a EUR 500-700 monthly stipend covers for 10-11 months; dormitory places are available only in limited numbers
document_audit: The confirmation letter must come from the institution's designated contact person on VIAA's unified template - a generic admission letter will be rejected
First-year master's applicants must additionally upload the bachelor's diploma copy and its supplement, not just current enrolment records
Proof of education can be a transcript of the last two semesters if studies are not yet completed
Recommendation letters must bear signatures dated within the last six months of the upload date
The study plan must use VIAA's own form, not a free-text document
A copy of the passport or ID card is required by the underlying Cabinet Regulation alongside the seven documents listed on the scholarship page
alerts: One application per open call: a wasted or defective submission cannot be replaced during the same round
No scholarship is paid for any month in which you are present in Latvia for fewer than 15 calendar days
Holding any other grant concurrently disqualifies the award
The stipend can be received for a maximum of two terms within one study cycle; continuing beyond that requires new funding
Decisions arrive by e-mail around June with the academic year starting 1 September - check spam folders and your system profile, as the lead time is short for visas and travel
If your country nominates candidates through an education authority, you may need to route documents through that authority as well
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Register online, complete the form against the published criteria, upload all translated documents into scholarships.viaa.gov.lv, and submit before 1 April; the system e-mails a confirmation and VIAA sends the decision by e-mail in June
